description: A five-panel composite figure of SEM (secondary-electron) fractographs of tensile-tested low-density Fe-28Mn-8Al-1C steel, each panel labelled (a)-(e) with a 10 µm scale bar in the lower-right corner. (a) is the undeformed condition: large, deep, open dimples separated by thick tearing ridges, the classic dimple-controlled ductile-fracture morphology, with one prominent deep central void. (b), (c) and (d) are the cryogenic-rolled (CR) conditions at 30%, 50% and 70% reduction; as CR increases the dimple network becomes progressively finer, denser, more uniform and shallower, and the large deep voids of (a) disappear. (e), CR 90%, is the finest of all: the surface is a dense mat of very small, shallow dimples with no large voids and a vertical crack/tear line running down the centre of the field. Together the panels argue that increasing cryogenic-rolling strain progressively refines and shallows the dimples while the fracture stays dimple-controlled (ductile), consistent with a loss of ductility with deformation. Only the 10 µm scale bar is numerically printed; no dimple-size values are annotated.
measured_quantities: dimple morphology / dimple size scale (µm, via 10 µm scale bar)

observations.observation: Panel (a), the undeformed condition, shows large and deep dimples separated by tearing ridges, the morphology the citing text calls characteristic of ductile fracture.
The citing text states that in the undeformed state (Figure 9a) distinctive large and deep dimples characteristic of ductile fracture are apparent.
From (b) to (e) the dimples become progressively finer, denser and shallower as the cryogenic-rolling reduction increases from 30% to 90%.
The large deep voids visible in (a) are absent in (e); the CR 90% fracture surface is a dense mat of very small, shallow dimples.
Panel (e) contains a vertical crack/tear line running down the centre of the imaged field, which is not present in panels (a)-(d).
Every panel carries a 10 µm scale bar in its lower-right corner and a panel letter (a)-(e) in its upper-left corner.
The caption identifies the five panels as undeformed, CR 30%, CR 50%, CR 70% and CR 90% respectively.
All five panels show dimple morphology, so the fracture remains dimple-controlled (ductile) across the whole CR series; only the dimple scale changes.
No numerical dimple size, dimple density or quantitative image-analysis value is printed on any panel; the only numeric label is the 10 µm scale bar.

subfigures.description: SEM fractograph of the undeformed steel with a 10 µm scale bar; shows large, deep, open dimples with thick tearing ridges and one prominent deep central void, characteristic of ductile fracture.
SEM fractograph, 10 µm scale bar, of the CR 30% condition; a network of dimples that are smaller and more numerous than in (a), with less prominent deep voids.
SEM fractograph, 10 µm scale bar, of the CR 50% condition; uniformly distributed dimples of reduced size and depth relative to (a) and (b).
SEM fractograph, 10 µm scale bar, of the CR 70% condition; fine, dense, relatively shallow dimples with a more homogeneous appearance.

SEM fractograph, 10 µm scale bar, of the CR 90% condition; the finest dimple structure of the series, very small shallow dimples with no large voids and a vertical crack/tear line through the centre of the field.
